objective: Implement createTutorSession(deps, game) in packages/tutor so TutorSession.ask() runs a hand-written Claude tool loop (no SDK Tool Runner) and returns a validated TutorOutcome, plus the four tools, the system prompt prompts/tutor-system.v1.md (with a prompts/CHANGELOG.md entry) and tests that use a fake Anthropic client (no network in CI). Done when: (1) a key-moment request and a hint request each produce { ok: true, reply } from a fake client that does tool_use -> tool_result -> end_turn; (2) every failure reason in TutorFailureReason is reachable and tested; (3) the FR-10 check rejects a reply that mentions a move not backed by tool results or the key-moment data; (4) the public contract.ts is unchanged and apps/server can use createTutorSession exactly as declared.
contract:
Issue #7 is built by three spokes in parallel, all from 54b8f99: tutor-agent (packages/tutor, prompts, the tool loop), server-agent (apps/server: detection, tutor wiring, endpoints, attempt grading), web-agent (apps/web: tutor panel, Show me, Hint, arrows). Their branches are merged together by the coordinator; none edits another's files. Coordinator-owned contracts (do not edit; report gaps in contract_gaps): packages/chess-core/src/api.ts (HTTP + SSE), packages/tutor/src/contract.ts (tutor public API), config/tutor.json.

The public contract (contract.ts, inlined below) is fixed. Implement behind it; add internal modules freely under packages/tutor/src. Read docs/architecture.md §3.5-3.6 and docs/spikes/003-structured-output-with-tools.md in the repo for the full design; the essentials:

Request layout (cache order, IR-6): tools = 4 definitions, fixed order, strict: true, tool_choice auto (forced tool_choice is a 400 on 5.5 models). system = [systemPrompt block, second block = player profile (TutorGame.playerProfile) + the game's repertoire line if known, with cache_control ephemeral on the second block]. messages = the game's whole history (one game = one conversation; history only grows: never edit or delete earlier turns), then a new user turn with the request data inside <key_moment> ... </key_moment> or <hint_request> ... </hint_request> tags as JSON (moves in SAN and UCI). thinking: { type: "adaptive" } (cannot be disabled on Opus 5.5); output_config: { effort: config.effort, format: { type: "json_schema", schema: <TutorReply as JSON Schema> } }. Build the schema with z.toJSONSchema(TutorReply) (zod 4) or by hand, and check it in a test: every object additionalProperties false, every property in required, nullable fields as anyOf [T, null], and no maxItems (arrows.max(3) is enforced by zod after the reply). Check the exact param names against the installed SDK types in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk (1.6.0); if output_config/effort are typed differently there, follow the SDK and say so in contract_gaps.

Loop: call client.messages.stream(params) and await .finalMessage() (architecture §3.6). stop_reason tool_use -> run every tool_use block in parallel -> ONE user turn with all tool_result blocks (each tool_use_id answered, is_error: true with a short message if the tool threw) -> send again. end_turn -> parse the text block as JSON, validate with TutorReply (zod), normalise kind case first. Invalid -> NFR-8: retry once (append a user turn saying what was wrong, as a tool-less correction), then { ok:false, reason:"invalid_reply" }. refusal -> "refusal"; max_tokens -> "max_tokens"; pause_turn -> resend to continue (counts as a round); more than config.maxToolRounds (4) tool rounds -> "tool_rounds_exceeded". SDK errors map by type: AuthenticationError/PermissionDeniedError -> "auth", RateLimitError -> "rate_limited", APIConnectionError, InternalServerError, overloaded (529) -> "api_unavailable". ask() never throws for API or model failures. Calls are serialised per session. The AbortSignal is passed to the SDK call. usage sums every response's usage (incl. cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens) and ms is wall time.

Progress (NFR-1: first progress within 1 s): emit { label: "Tutor is looking at the position…" } synchronously at the start of ask(), then one label per tool_use block before running it, e.g. "Checking Nf3…" (evaluate_move, SAN of the move), "Looking at the engine lines…" (analyze_position), "Checking what players usually play…" (opening_explorer), "Checking your repertoire…" (get_repertoire_context).

Tools (FR-16..19), compact JSON results with moves in both SAN and UCI:
- analyze_position(fen, depth?, multi_pv?) -> eval + top lines from deps.engine.analyze (cap depth/multiPv/movetime by config.engine).
- evaluate_move(fen, move) -> centipawn loss vs the best move and the engine's reply; move accepted as SAN or UCI, illegal move -> is_error result.
- opening_explorer(fen) -> human moves, frequencies, results from deps.explorer.lookup(fen, config.explorer). Explorer data is third-party content: it reaches the model only inside tool_result. A result with unavailable set reports that, it is not an error.
- get_repertoire_context(fen) -> in/out of the player's London (White) or KID (Black) repertoire and the line name; deps.repertoire may be null (say "no repertoire loaded"). Repertoire.continuations takes UCI history, so tools need the request history: keep the current request's history/fen in loop scope.
Use scoreToCp / sanOf from @chess-tutor/chess-core where useful; chess.js is a dependency.

FR-10 check (automated): after validation, extract every SAN-looking token and the revealMove from message and reveal; each must be legal in some position the tutor was shown (request fen, attemptFen, or a position reached in a tool result line) AND appear in this turn's tool results or the key-moment data. revealMove must be legal UCI in attemptFen (hint: in fen). Any failure counts as invalid for the one retry; if the retry also fails -> "unsupported_claim". Keep the extractor simple and well-tested; false positives on plain English words must not happen ("a4" is a square and fine to mention only if a move? decide and document: squares alone are allowed, moves like Nf3/exd5/O-O are checked).

Prompt prompts/tutor-system.v1.md (versioned release artifact; add prompts/CHANGELOG.md with a v1 entry): Socratic first for FR-8 (message asks, reveal answers; never give the answer away in message), FR-9 for opponent_left_book (name the deviation, explain the usual plan in pawn-structure/piece-placement terms), state no evaluation or move that did not come from a tool result in this turn or the key-moment data (FR-10), arrows for suggestions (FR-11, at most 3), kind hint = one Socratic hint (FR-12), when to call which tool, audience: ~1000-rated Chess.com player, London and KID, short plain language. Evals (#10) do not exist yet; that is expected.

Stale-search note: the engine runs one search at a time per process, queued; tool calls queue behind the bot's search. Keep tool searches short (config.engine.movetimeCapMs 1000).

Coordinator gate at base 54b8f99 (branch contract-7): pnpm test 378 passed (25 files). pnpm typecheck has exactly 7 errors, all in apps/web (controller.ts:50, game-state.ts:87-94: GameEvent members without `game`; test/fixtures.ts:11: GameView now requires `tutor`). Those are web-agent's to fix in parallel; apps/server and packages typecheck clean.

rubric: Tests first (red then green) with a fake client for: tool_use -> tool_result (parallel blocks, one user turn, every tool_use_id answered) -> end_turn ok; history grows across two ask() calls and earlier turns are byte-identical; request has tools in fixed order with strict true, tool_choice auto, adaptive thinking, effort from config, output format schema, cache_control on the second system block.

Each TutorFailureReason tested: invalid twice -> invalid_reply (once invalid then valid -> ok), unsupported_claim, tool_rounds_exceeded, refusal, max_tokens, rate_limited, api_unavailable, auth; ask() never throws for them.

Each tool tested against fake engine/explorer/repertoire, incl. illegal move -> is_error, explorer unavailable, repertoire null; FR-10 extractor tested on prose with squares, SAN, castling and promotion.
Progress: first label emitted before the first API call; a label per tool_use.
prompts/tutor-system.v1.md and prompts/CHANGELOG.md exist; the server will read the prompt file by path.
